slides.title: How it works
slides.html: Admins set up every phone, and you send your marks to others' Inbox. Ask a plugin such as Drones to act on a target, and its updates arrive in yours.

slides.title: Admins and users
slides.html: Deploy App, the service that enrols your phone on the TAK server, makes some users admins. Admins start with the Setting up chapter, everyone else with Starting as a user.

slides.title: Your phone and the operation
slides.html: Every soldier sets their own phone under THIS PHONE, such as My unit and Enemy near me. Only admins change what OPERATION shows.

slides.title: ORBAT
slides.html: The ORBAT, the order of battle, lists the operation's units, each under the one it belongs to. Admins build it, and until then phones use a built-in Finnish rifle company.

slides.title: Your unit
slides.html: Your unit, picked from the ORBAT, decides which area the Inbox watches. It also decides which feeds you should follow, the TAK server's shared lists of marks.

slides.title: Admin settings
slides.html: Admins set up the operation under Server configuration (admins), which only they see in the OpenDefence Main pane. Once they publish, every phone takes the setup.

slides.title: Favourites
slides.html: Admins pick up to 12 favourite symbols for each side. Markers offers them first when you pick a symbol.

slides.title: Usual targets
slides.html: Admins set each unit's Usual targets, where its marks usually go. The card after placing a mark then sends there in one tap.

slides.title: Markers
slides.html: Markers, on the thumb bar at the map's bottom left, places what you see or plan in a few taps. Each mark carries a military symbol every TAK user reads.

slides.title: What you can mark
slides.html: A mark can be a unit, a position, a route or an area, friendly, neutral, unknown or enemy. Friendly units come from the ORBAT.

slides.title: Sending a mark
slides.html: A new mark stays on your phone and reads NOT SENT. Send to… shares it to a feed, a role such as HQ, or another plugin.

slides.title: Stale and fresh markers
slides.html: Enemy reports get old, and the enemy may have moved since. A neutral, unknown or enemy mark goes stale after the time admins set, 24 hours unless they change it.

slides.title: Stale on the map
slides.html: A fresh mark's label says how old it is, such as 3 h ago. A stale one turns grey and reads Stale.

slides.title: Inbox
slides.html: The Inbox, at the top of the thumb bar, gathers what others report. Its red count says how many items are new.

slides.title: Closest first
slides.html: The Inbox lists the closest enemy first: Close, under 500 m, then Near you, then your unit's area.

slides.title: Requests
slides.html: A request asks another OpenDefence plugin to act on a mark or a drawn area. OpenDefence UAVOps, opened with Drones, takes requests for a drone strike or recon.

slides.title: The target button
slides.html: Tap the mark or area, then the target button, a crosshair in ATAK's ring of buttons. It is there only when the phone has a plugin that takes requests.

slides.title: Following a request
slides.html: You follow your request under Sent in the Inbox. Those you asked find it under For you.

slides.title: Open for new plugins
slides.html: Other OpenDefence plugins, each its own app, join OpenDefence Main where you already look. OpenDefence Voice and OpenDefence Matrix also work alone, but OpenDefence UAVOps needs OpenDefence Main.

slides.title: Where plugins join in
slides.html: Plugins add buttons such as Drones and Voice, rows in Send to… and the Inbox, choices on the Request sheet and admin settings such as Quotas and corridors.

slides.title: Built and signed the same way
slides.html: Every plugin is built and checked the same way, and TAK.gov signs it. Plugins to come, such as Fires, Logistics and Sensors, join the same way.
